framing: A marketplace with web, mobile, and operations surfaces needs one booking state—and a recovery path when any client disconnects.
challenge: Booking status could drift between web and mobile clients after a dropped connection. The same product also had to carry payments, notifications, verification, and fulfilment across customer, worker, admin, and background-verification surfaces.
ownership: Sole technical owner across the five-app monorepo: customer and worker web, Expo mobile, API, and operational applications.
Owned 50+ Express routes spanning auth, payments, notifications, booking state, and reconciliation between payment webhooks and internal records.
Owned delivery concerns as well as feature work: Docker images, pre-merge type-check and lint gates, and a tested rollback path.

decisions.title: Make reconnect a normal path
decisions.body: Rebuilt booking updates around Socket.IO and Redis Pub/Sub with idempotent retries, so a client can catch up after a dropped connection instead of polling on a timer.

decisions.title: Keep durable state authoritative
decisions.body: PostgreSQL remains the system of record while Redis supports fast-moving operational state and Socket.IO carries live updates.

decisions.title: Cover the closed-app case
decisions.body: Added push notifications alongside Socket.IO because a customer may need a booking update when the app is not open.

decisions.title: Treat discovery through confirmation as one flow
decisions.body: Rebuilt the customer frontend in Next.js with server-side rendering and an SEO layer because most new customers were arriving through search, carrying the path through checkout and payment confirmation.

evidence: Customer and worker web/mobile clients share the same service and data layer for booking and fulfilment state.
The deployment path covers five applications with containerized builds and a rollback path that has been tested.
The live product is available at zaruro.com; customer-volume and revenue metrics are not published here.
boundary: Evidence is limited to shipped product behavior, the public product surface, and resume-backed engineering records. No private customer or revenue metrics are inferred.
